title: feat(landing): ask for support on the download page, in the page's own voice
body:
The request was "add the sponsor URL to the download page". The page has had one all along — `SiteFooter` renders `♥ sponsor`, fourteenth of fourteen links. So the premise was already satisfied, and the actual gap was different: there was no **ask**, only a link. Nothing connected "you just got something useful for free" to "here is how to support it".

> That unsigned-app warning is a **code-signing certificate I can't afford yet**. If this earns its keep → GitHub Sponsors · PayPal · Ko-fi

## Placement

After the install notes, not beside the download buttons.

By that point the page has given the visitor everything it promised, so the ask reads as *"if it works out"* rather than a toll gate on a free download. It also puts distance between the ask and the lede's **"No accounts, no upsell, no tracking."** A tip jar is not the upsell that line disclaims — but a skim-reader four lines away might not grant the distinction, and the alternative placement (after the extension section) would have stacked it about two centimetres above the footer's own `♥ sponsor`, ending the page with the same ask twice.

## Why this angle

The page already tells you twice that the app is unsigned because the author has no money, and every platform card below carries the OS warning that follows from it. Pointing the ask at the certificate makes it the one framing where **paying visibly benefits the payer** — it buys the thing that removes the friction they are reading about right now. A specific reason converts where a generic plea does not.

## Two deliberate absences in the copy

- **No price.** Certificate costs change, and a number committed to a public page is a number that silently becomes a lie — precisely the failure `scripts/check-landing-drift.mjs` exists to catch.
- **No positional reference.** An earlier draft said *"the warning above"*. That is meaningless in a screen reader's linear read (WCAG 1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics, which the `/accessibility` statement claims partial conformance with), and it is not even reliably true: those warnings live in per-button notes that `DownloadFreshness` rewrites at runtime and that reflow on narrow viewports. Name the thing, never its position.

## Destinations

All three, ordered **GitHub Sponsors → PayPal → Ko-fi**. The footer already covers the Sponsors-only case, and the likely donor for a free unsigned app drops a fiver once rather than starting a recurring sponsorship.

Reuses `.auto-note` (mono, muted) — no new CSS.

## Verification

- `pnpm -F @ajh/landing exec vitest run` — 37 files / 342 tests pass
- `pnpm check:landing-drift` — passes; it reads this exact file for claim drift
- `pnpm lint:strict --max-warnings 0`, `pnpm -F @ajh/landing typecheck` — clean
- Rendered in a browser and visually checked against the surrounding page

**All three new assertions are mutation-checked**, not merely green — reordering the links, restoring "above", and naming a price each fail exactly one test and nothing else.

## Not verified

`ko-fi.com` returns HTTP 200 for a username I invented, so its status code cannot confirm the account exists. `KOFI` is already live on the home page via `Finale.tsx`, so this adds no new risk — but if that account is not set up, it is now wrong in two places.

## Unrelated observation

Running `pnpm -F @ajh/landing dev` generates untracked `apps/landing/AGENTS.md` and `apps/landing/CLAUDE.md` (Next.js `agentRules`). They are not gitignored. Removed rather than committed here, but anyone running the dev server will keep rediscovering them.
